kendal.snapshot: Kendal is a south Cumbrian market town where full fibre is going in alongside a long tail of broadband, CCTV and structured-cabling installers. Build contractors field whole crews and order through trade accounts and central procurement, while ex-BT sole traders and one-van installers across the town take just a few branded pieces and order direct online with no account. A workwear supplier here has to serve the fleet and the lone engineer alike.
kendal.s1_head: Kitting the field engineers of south Cumbria
s1loc: Kendal sits in the middle of a real Cumbrian full fibre push. Openreach has run FTTP out across much of the town under the Connecting Cumbria and Project Gigabit work, while alt-net Fibrus is building its own gigabit network through Kendal, aiming at thousands of homes and businesses, and is laying fibre across nearby Penrith, Workington and Aspatria too. The result is delivery partners and civils crews working through districts like Kirkland, Sandylands, Oxenholme and Burneside, pulling fibre to the cabinet and on to the premises across the town's streets.

Around the residential build sits Kendal's commercial scene. The Mintsfeet and Mintbridge industrial estates, the K Village and Lound Road areas and the town's business units host firms that need structured cabling and CCTV - offices, schools, the hospital and multi-site operators wired in Cat5e, Cat6 and fibre. With Kendal College, the auction mart and a steady flow of tourism and manufacturing premises across the Kent valley, local cabling and security installers take on a constant run of fit-outs, upgrades and maintenance jobs across south Cumbria.

malvern.s1_head: Kitting the field engineers of Worcestershire
s1loc: Malvern is on Openreach's full fibre upgrade list, with FTTP being built out across the town, while alt-nets are active across Worcestershire - Airband running ultrafast fibre and fixed wireless into the Malvern Hills area and Gigaclear reaching selected premises around the town. Under the Superfast Worcestershire and Project Gigabit work, contractor and civils crews push fibre through Great Malvern, Barnards Green, Malvern Link, Poolbrook and West Malvern, pulling cable to the cabinet and on into homes and businesses across the foot of the hills.

Around that cluster, the Spring Lane and Enigma estates and the town's schools, hospital and offices keep local cabling and security installers busy with Cat6 and fibre fit-outs across Malvern and the county.
